pages.title: Now it's your turn
pages.subtext: Solve a fresh weighted graph. We will guide you when needed.
pages.cardText: Start at vertex A. Find the lowest-cost route to D using Dijkstra's algorithm.
pages.tipText: Observe → answer → check → learn from feedback.

contentBox.text: Weighted graph with nodes A, B, C, D.

pages.title: Set the starting values
pages.subtext: Before exploring, initialise your distance table.
pages.cardTitle: What is the distance to the source A?
pages.correctFeedback: The distance to the starting node itself is always 0.
pages.incorrectFeedback: The source node starts with a distance of 0.

pages.title: Explore A's neighbours
pages.subtext: A has distance 0. Its edges reach B and C.
pages.cardTitle: What tentative distance should B receive?
pages.correctFeedback: Tentative distance is source distance plus edge weight (0 + 2 = 2).

pages.title: Choose the next vertex
pages.subtext: A is done. The unsettled distances are B: 2, C: 5, D: ∞.
pages.correctFeedback: B has the smallest tentative distance (2) among unsettled vertices.
pages.incorrectFeedback: Always pick the unsettled vertex with the minimum tentative distance.

pages.title: Find a shorter way to C
pages.subtext: Current distance C = 5. B has distance 2; B–C weighs 1.
pages.correctFeedback: Since 3 < 5, we update C's distance to 3.
pages.incorrectFeedback: New path through B gives 2 + 1 = 3, which is shorter than 5.

pages.title: Record a predecessor
pages.subtext: B has distance 2 and its edge to D weighs 6.
pages.cardTitle: What are D's new distance and predecessor?
pages.incorrectFeedback: Add B's distance (2) to edge weight (6) to get 8.

pages.title: Find the next minimum
pages.subtext: Unsettled: C: 3 and D: 8. Choose the smallest.
pages.correctFeedback: C has distance 3, which is smaller than D's distance 8.
pages.incorrectFeedback: Compare tentative distances of unsettled vertices.

pages.title: Improve D through C
pages.subtext: C has distance 3; its edge to D weights 2.
pages.correctFeedback: 5 < 8, so we update D's distance to 5 and set predecessor to C.
pages.incorrectFeedback: Since 5 is shorter than 8, update D's distance and predecessor.

pages.title: Rebuild the path
pages.subtext: The final predecessor chain is D ← C ← B ← A.
pages.incorrectFeedback: Follow the chain backwards from D to A.

pages.title: You've run Dijkstra!
pages.subtext: You solved the graph from A to D.
pages.tipText: For independent assessment you'll solve an unfamiliar graph.
